precepts.text: Glory not in the dishonour of thy father. Some of you who are older may have parents that are not in this truth, and you might think you don't have to give them the respect of a parent. That's not what the Lord said. My son, help thy father in his age: you are to be an aid to your parent at a certain age, and not just when you feel like it. If his understanding fail, have patience with him. Notice we're the only nation of people that don't take care of our elders; where do you think nursing homes come from? Deacon: I have a real disdain for children that do not honor their parents, because mine died when I was young and I went through the system with no mother and father. To have them, and be able to have a conversation with them, and still not respect that: that's a problem for me.
precepts.point: And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. That's the judgment for not honoring your father and mother.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
“Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.” Some who are older have parents who are not in this truth, and they might think that because their parent is not in the truth they do not have to give them the respect of a parent. That is not what the Lord said. It is no glory that your father or mother is not in this truth, and nothing to glory in because the Lord called you.

“For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father; and a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.”

“My son, help thy father in his age, and grieve him not as long as he liveth.” You are to be an aid to your parent when they reach a certain age, and not just when you feel like it. “And if his understanding fail, have patience with him”. We are the only nation of people that does not take care of our elders. Where do you think nursing homes come from? The children do not want to deal with their parents at a certain age, so they pay somebody else to watch after them. That is how we honour our parents.

The Deacon has a real disdain for children who do not honour their parents, because his died when he was young and he went through the system with no mother and father, though his grandparents took him in. To have your parents, and be able to have a conversation with them, and still not respect that: that is a problem.

“And despise him not when thou art in thy full strength.” Be patient, because the example we set is what the young men see; we are their goalpost.

precepts.text: Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn. That is why the camp teaches God's laws without going left or right; we know we got here through stubbornness.
precepts.point: A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last, and he that loveth danger shall perish therein. We have to prophesy against the idolatry and come out of Christmas, Valentine's Day and the rest that God never gave us.
precepts.why:
The Lord clothed us and named us, yet even in 2026 our people are still worshiping the devil, giving gifts to the sea goddess. And we wonder why America is going down there stealing presidents, starving people out and destabilizing countries. “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” We have to prophesy against the idolatry and come up out of this foolishness: Christmas, Valentine’s Day, which a lot of our people celebrated. That has nothing to do with us. God did not give that to us.

Sirach shows where stubbornness is dealt with: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart.”

That is why we teach God’s laws the way we do. We are not going to the left or to the right with any of you. We are not playing games, because we know why we got over here. We know how we got here: through stubbornness. So if we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

Judges shows how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them”, and “they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no leader in place, when the officer, the captain, the deacon or the bishop isn’t there, they go back to their lonesome. If you cannot uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction. A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last.

precepts.text: Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence. And we what? And we gave them reverence. What is another term for reverence? Respect. Honour. Shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits? So now even more so we have got to respect the Lord that created us, even more so. But we still have to have respect and honour and reverence for our earthly fathers. Thus saith the Lord.
precepts.point: You make an atonement for your sins when you do that. When you honour your father, that wipes away your sins. Let us see why.
precepts.why:
“Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins”, and that goes for your mother too. When you honour your father, that wipes away your sins. Hebrews shows why.

“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence”. Another word for reverence is respect, honour. The fathers of our flesh corrected us and we gave them that honour.

“Shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” So even more so we have to respect the Lord that created us. But that does not cancel the first part: we still have to have respect, honour and reverence for our earthly fathers. Thus saith the Lord. Honouring the father of your flesh is part of being in subjection to the Father of spirits, and that is why it makes an atonement.

precepts.text: And it does not matter if they are a repentant Israelite or if they are in the world. You still have got to respect and honour them either way. Because remember, we have got to let our light shine. We have got to be the light to the Gentiles, the unrepentant of our people. Because at one point you were unrepentant too. As we have therefore opportunity — so as much as this opportunity arises — let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith. So we have got to do good to all men, those in the truth and those out of the truth. That goes back to Romans when it says live peaceably with all men.
precepts.point: You make an atonement for your sins when you do that. When you honour your father, that wipes away your sins. Let us see why.
precepts.why:
Honouring your father and mother does not depend on whether they are a repentant Israelite or still in the world. You still have to respect and honour them either way.

We have to let our light shine and be the light to the Gentiles, the unrepentant of our people, because at one point you were unrepentant too. Paul says, “As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.” As much as the opportunity arises, we do good to all men, those in the truth and those out of the truth, and that includes the parents who raised us.

That goes back to Romans, where it says live peaceably with all men. So when Sirach says “Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins”, it is not only the father who is in the faith; doing good to your parents wherever they stand is the honour that brings that atonement.

precepts.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt. So the treasures on earth — crypto coins, Bitcoin, the computers could blow up, money is going to burn, gold could melt — and where thieves break through and steal. Somebody could steal it. But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven. But the treasure we should lay up is what? The treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt. Because the treasure in heaven, that eternal life we are all striving for, nothing can take that away from us once we achieve it. And where thieves do not break through nor steal. No thieves can break through and get those things, what the Lord has prepared for us in paradise. No thief can take that away from us once we attain it. But we have got to get there.
precepts.point: Now, we are not talking about gold or diamonds or crypto or NFTs. Let us see what type of treasure the Bible is talking about that you lay up for yourself when you honour your father and respect your mother.
precepts.why:
Sirach says “he that honoureth his mother is as one that layeth up treasure.” We are not talking about gold or diamonds or crypto or NFTs. Christ shows what kind of treasure it is.

“Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. The treasures on earth, crypto coins and Bitcoin, can go when the computers blow up; money is going to burn; gold can melt; somebody can steal it.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal”. The treasure in heaven is the eternal life we are all striving for. Nothing can take that away from us once we attain it, and no thief can break through and get what the Lord has prepared for us in paradise.

So honouring and respecting your mother is laying up that treasure in heaven. But we have got to get there.

precepts.text: Now we know that God heareth not sinners. Now, this is clear and plain. Now we know, everybody knows, that God heareth not sinners. So when we are in habitual, presumptuous sin, the Lord is not going to hear our prayers.
precepts.point: So when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard. So why does it say that? It means when you are not honouring your father or your mother, your prayers are not going to be heard. Showing that it is a commandment to honour your parents. Why is that? Why will your prayers not be heard?
precepts.why:
“Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children; and when he maketh his prayer, he shall be heard.” Why does it say that? It means that when you are not honouring your father or your mother, your prayers are not going to be heard, which shows that honouring your parents is a commandment.

John makes it clear and plain: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners”. Everybody knows it. Dishonouring your parents is breaking a commandment, and a sinner is not heard.

So when we are in habitual, presumptuous sin, the Lord is not going to hear our prayers. The one who honours his father is keeping the commandment, and that is why, when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.

precepts.text: Obey them that have the rule over you. So the Bible says obey them that have the rule over you. Plain and simple. And submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls. For these people watch for our souls. Even though in the past, when you were not in the truth, your parents watched out for your life and your safety and well-being, even though before they knew the truth. They cared for you all up until the time where you were able to repent and now be a commandment-keeping Israelite. So have respect and honour for them.
precepts.point: The same way we have respect for our elders, for the men over us, or whoever you report to, you need to have that same respect or more for your parents as well too, because they brought you into this world.
precepts.why:
“He that feareth the Lord will honour his father, and will do service unto his parents, as to his masters.” The same respect you have for your boss, your employer, whoever gainfully employs you, the elders and the men over you, you should have for your parents and more, because they brought you into this world.

Hebrews says it plain and simple: “Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls”. These people watch for our souls.

Your parents did that too. Even in the past, before they or you knew the truth, they watched out for your life, your safety and your well-being. They cared for you all the way up to the time you were able to repent and become a commandment-keeping Israelite. So have respect and honour for them, and do service unto them as to your masters.

precepts.text: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children. So a good man will leave an inheritance to his what? To his children's children. What is that? That is talking about grandchildren. So if you have a good relationship with your family members and your mother and your parents, you never know. They could be saving money for your children, for their college tuition. They could be leaving that blessing for you just because of the way you conduct yourself and the way you treated them with respect. But if you are acting up and you are being disrespectful to them and you are not letting your light shine as an Israelite should, they are not going to deal with you. So you are not even going to see it. They are not going to help you with the baby when stuff comes. They are not going to help you get that stroller. They are not going to wash the kids for you. They are not going to do none of those things for you if you are not honouring and reverencing them.
precepts.point: How can the blessings of a father establish children? Let us see. But you can only get this blessing if you are honouring and respecting your parents and doing what the Lord says to do.
precepts.why:
“Honour thy father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon thee from them.” Both in word and deed means whatever you say, do it. The blessing comes from them, and “the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children.” How can the blessing of a father establish children? Solomon shows it: “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children.”

Children's children are grandchildren. So if you have a good relationship with your family, with your mother and your parents, you never know: they could be saving money for your children, for their college tuition. They could be leaving that blessing for you just because of the way you conduct yourself and the way you treated them with respect.

But you only get that blessing if you are honouring and respecting your parents and doing what the Lord says to do. If you are acting up and being disrespectful to them, and not letting your light shine as an Israelite should, they are not going to deal with you, and you will never even see it. They are not going to help you with the baby when stuff comes. They are not going to help you get that stroller. They are not going to wash the kids for you. They are not going to do none of those things if you are not honouring and reverencing them.

That is how the father's blessing establishes the houses of children: honour him in word and deed, and his inheritance reaches down to your own children.

precepts.text: Children's children are the crown of old men. So it says children's children, grandchildren are the crown, and great-grandkids are the crown of old men. They want to see you have children and keep procreating. They see, like, dang, you came from me, now you are creating life again. Man, I would love to see that thing. Parents love seeing that. And the glory of children are their fathers. So if your father is in dishonour, that means you are in dishonour too. So there is no glory in that. That is why we have got to let our light shine.
precepts.point: For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father. For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father. And a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children. And a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.
precepts.why:
“Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.” Oh, my dad, yeah man, he is broke, he is a bum now, my mom left him behind. That is no glory to you. You came from him. “For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father.” Solomon says the same: “Children’s children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.”

Children's children, the grandchildren, and the great-grandkids are the crown of old men. They want to see you have children and keep procreating. They see it and say, dang, you came from me, and now you are creating life again. Man, I would love to see that. Parents love seeing that.

And the glory of children are their fathers. So if your father is in dishonour, you are in dishonour too. There is no glory in that, and “a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.” The honour of the parents and the honour of the children are tied together, one generation to the next.

That is why we have got to let our light shine: so our fathers are honoured in us, and we become a crown to them.

precepts.text: Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? Why trimmest thou thy ways to seek love? We cannot trim our ways as far as keeping the commandments, to seek love and affection and acceptance from our family members. Therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways. Because when we do that, we are teaching our family members to be wicked. We say, oh no, I am not going to do x, y and z. But they say, hey, come do this with us. And you cave in. You show them you are not really about the word of God.
precepts.point: Now, does that mean my mom is mad at me because I am not coming to the Christmas party? Are you in sin for that? I did not come over for Mother's Day and get her a bouquet of flowers. Let us see.
precepts.why:
Sirach warns that “he that angereth his mother is cursed: of God.” Does that mean you are in sin because your mom is mad you are not coming to the Christmas party, or because you did not come over for Mother’s Day with a bouquet of flowers? Jeremiah answers it.

“Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love?” We cannot trim our ways in keeping the commandments to seek love, affection and acceptance from our family members.

“Therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.” When we do that, we teach our family members to be wicked. We say we are not going to do this or that, then they say, come do this with us, and we cave in. That shows them we are not really about the word of God.

So honouring your parents is helping your father in his age, having patience with him when his understanding fails, not despising him when you are in your full strength. It is not trimming the commandments to keep the peace at their holidays.

precepts.text: Be not curious in unnecessary matters; think with reverence on what is commanded thee.
precepts.point: Do not go seeking books he did not command us to read: the book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. There are enough deep mysteries in the eighty books he gave us, the sixty-six and the books of the Apocrypha, to stay focused on.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“Seek not out things that are too hard for thee, neither search the things that are above thy strength. But what is commanded thee, think thereupon with reverence, for it is not needful for thee to see with thine eyes the things that are in secret.” Think with reverence on what is commanded thee: the book of the Lord that his spirit gathered, not the book of Jasher he left out.

“Be not curious in unnecessary matters: for more things are shewed unto thee than men understand. For many are deceived by their own vain opinion; and an evil suspicion hath overthrown their judgment.” The book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. More is shewed in the eighty books he gave us than men understand; stay focused on those.

precepts.text: Obstinate is another word for stubborn: the mind set on doing what it wants contrary to counsel will be laden with sorrows, and Saul heaped sin upon sin, lying, justifying himself, and blaming the people, which is what carried him into the witchcraft and idolatry of rebellion.
precepts.point: This stubborn heart is what fares evil at the last; we will read Saul's end in the last chapter of 1 Samuel, and in chapter 16 the evil spirit enters into him and the Spirit of the Lord departs. The plant of wickedness took root here.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” That is heavy. A brother who would never touch voodoo will sit through a whole counsel of do not do this, and call two weeks later saying he did it anyway; according to this verse, that rebellion is the same as witchcraft.

Stubbornness is idolatry because the instruction does not come from the man; it is the commandment of the Lord that leadership carries. When you are stubborn against it, you are saying what I want to do comes before what God wants me to do, and you have put yourself in the midst of idolatry as surely as circling the stone at Mecca or bowing before a cross. “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king”: you will lose whatever position the Most High put you in.

“A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein. An obstinate heart shall be laden with sorrows; and the wicked man shall heap sin upon sin.” Obstinate is another word for stubborn: the mind set on doing what it wants contrary to counsel will be laden with sorrows. Saul heaped sin upon sin, lying, justifying himself and blaming the people, and that is what carried him into the witchcraft and idolatry of rebellion.

This stubborn heart is what fares evil at the last. Saul’s end comes in the last chapter of 1 Samuel, and in chapter 16 the evil spirit enters into him and the Spirit of the Lord departs. The plant of wickedness took root here.

precepts.text: Humble yourself before the Most High and you find favour, and the mysteries are revealed to the meek and lowly, as they were to tender hearted Josiah.
precepts.point: But because Josiah's heart was tender and he humbled himself, wept, and rent his clothes, the Most High will gather him to his fathers in peace so his eyes will not see the evil to come.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“My son, go on with thy business in meekness; so shalt thou be beloved of him that is approved. The greater thou art, the more humble thyself, and thou shalt find favour before the Lord. Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed unto the meek. For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.”

Humble yourself before the Most High and you find favour, and the mysteries are revealed to the meek and lowly, as they were to tender-hearted Josiah. The king was great, and he humbled himself the more.

Huldah the prophetess declared evil upon Jerusalem, “even all the curses that are written in the book”, “Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense unto other gods”. But to the king: “Because thine heart was tender, and thou didst humble thyself before God, when thou heardest his words against this place”, “and didst rend thy clothes, and weep before me; I have even heard thee also, saith the Lord.” That is the favour found by the humble.

precepts.text: Go on with thy business in meekness; the greater thou art, the more humble thyself and find favor before the Most High.
precepts.point: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and a contrite heart, which the Most High will not despise. Contrite means meek and teachable.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” Contrite means meek and teachable. “My son, go on with thy business in meekness; so shalt thou be beloved of him that is approved.” The greater thou art, the more humble thyself, and thou shalt find favour before the Most High.

That meekness is the contrite heart. It is the sacrifice the Most High will not despise, and it makes you beloved.

precepts.text: Mysteries are revealed unto the meek.
precepts.point: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and a contrite heart, which the Most High will not despise. Contrite means meek and teachable.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: “Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed unto the meek.” Not to the high and renowned, but to the meek. A contrite heart is meek and teachable, and that is the heart the Most High reveals his mysteries to. That is why a broken and a contrite heart is the sacrifice he will not despise.

precepts.text: For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honored of the lowly.
precepts.point: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and a contrite heart, which the Most High will not despise. Contrite means meek and teachable.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: “For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.” The Most High is honoured by the lowly. A broken spirit and a contrite heart, meek and teachable, is what honours him, and that is the sacrifice of God he will not despise. The high and renowned do not honour him; the lowly do, and mysteries are revealed to them.

precepts.text: Seek not the things too hard for thee; think on what is commanded with reverence, not curious in unnecessary matters.
precepts.point: Many babes fall because instead of consuming the milk they try to go straight for the meat. The teaching is about brothers and sisters who reach for things a little too hard.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why:
David says his heart is not haughty nor his eyes lofty; he does not think he is better than anyone and is not proud above measure, and he does not exercise himself in great matters or in things too high for him. “Seek not out things that are too hard for thee, neither search the things that are above thy strength. But what is commanded thee, think thereupon with reverence, for it is not needful for thee to see with thine eyes the things that are in secret. Be not curious in unnecessary matters: for more things are shewed unto thee than men understand.”

Many babes fall because instead of consuming the milk they try to go straight for the meat. Brothers and sisters reach for things a little too hard, when what is commanded is to be thought upon with reverence.

precepts.text: We must not glory in a father's dishonor.
precepts.point: Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“Children’s children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.” Many of us grew up in fatherless homes, but “Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.”

We must not glory in a father’s dishonor. Sisters should not speak evil of the man they chose to lie down with and bring in seed by, no matter how bad he is; children raised to despise their fathers must repent of it in this truth.

Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

points: He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed of God. Now you have got to reflect back on the videos we have been looking at. One girl was beating the crap out of her mama. She is going to pay for that. You do not think the Lord is going to make that daughter pay for that?

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Many are in high place, and of renown. You have got people that are in powerful positions on this earth, and they are famous. But mysteries are revealed unto the meek. To the meek. Where are the meek of the earth? The Israelites. The mysteries of God have been revealed unto us. You have got people in high tech positions, high government, high as celebrity, basketball players, athletes. But mysteries are revealed unto the meek. God is dealing with us. He is going to reveal his stuff to us.

For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly. Seek not out things that are too hard for thee, neither search the things that are above thy strength. But what is commanded thee, think thereupon with reverence. He commanded us to keep the commandments and keep his covenant. Do we have to go no higher than that? He will give us everything else.

For it is not needful for thee to see with thine eyes the things that are in secret. There are things that God has to himself that are secret. We do not need to see it. That is why some of you all are into tarot cards. You all are into brujeria, chango, voodoo. Whatever it is in your island, wherever you come from, you want to see secret spiritual things. And all you have to do is just keep the commandments, keep the covenant. It is not needful to dig into that spiritual realm, because we have a God, the creator of all things, that will give you whatever you want.

Be not curious in unnecessary matters. Like Eve was in the garden. She was already in paradise, and Satan came and whispered something into her ear, and now she was curious. Maybe God lied to us. Maybe there is better than this. How could you look in paradise, you live in paradise, and you are saying, maybe there is something else? You are in paradise. You do not have none of the stuff to deal with that we are dealing with. And one day you wake up and you are like that.

For more things are shewed unto thee than men understand. We do not even understand the stuff that we see with our eyes, and you all are looking for deeper stuff to find out. That is why I laugh when people start bringing up the Illuminati and the secret societies. I do not care about that. It is going to burn when we get our turn. The Bible is the only thing we are supposed to learn. I do not care about no secret society. I do not care what the government is doing. The Lord is going to reveal everything and destroy them. We know something they do not know.

For many are deceived by their own vain opinion. Your own vain opinion is when you deviate from what is written in the scriptures. And an evil suspicion hath overthrown their judgment. That is what happened with Eve in the garden. She had an evil suspicion of God. Satan told her, if you go against God's instruction, your eyes will be opened and you will be wise.

Without eyes thou shalt want light: profess not the knowledge therefore that thou hast not. Satan came to her with knowledge that was not necessary for her. All she had to do was be obedient to the Lord.

A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last. Meaning you do not want to keep God's commandments, so eventually evil is going to come to your doorstep. And he that loveth danger shall perish therein. Some of you all like the life that you are living. Some of you all are coming to this truth and we are explaining to you why you should not be an adulterer, why you should not be an alcoholic, why you should not be a drug user, but you want to stay in a place of danger that goes against God.

An obstinate heart shall be laden with sorrows. Everything is going to go wrong for you because your heart is obstinate against God. You do not want to listen. That is why some people I do not give counsel to, after I spoke to them and I realise they are not listening. Your life is sorrow. You do not care about keeping the commandments. You do not care about breaking the covenant. So that is why your life is sorrow.
And the wicked man shall heap sin upon sin. In the punishment of the proud there is no remedy. Because in your own pride nothing could be done. God is punishing you and nothing is changing.

For the plant of wickedness hath taken root in him. It is like Satan planted a seed of wickedness in you and it has taken root. So all the punishment, all the captivity, everything that we showed to you is of no benefit to you. God sowed a righteous seed; Satan sowed a wicked seed inside of you. So there is no remedy for you. The scriptures cannot do nothing to help you.
The heart of the prudent will understand a parable; and an attentive ear is the desire of a wise man. Because the parables are mysteries. The heart of the prudent will discern these parables.

Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms maketh an atonement for sins. And he that requiteth good turns is mindful of that which may come hereafter. People do not understand that alms, which is assistance for your people, will make an atonement for your sins. That is a mystery. What are they doing when they give money in the church? They are giving it to the pastor and their life is still a disaster. That money is a waste. All of you in church giving your money, and the pastor is taking it to live a lavish lifestyle. You just wasted all your money.

Water will quench a flaming fire. When there is a fire, you pour water on it so the stuff does not get burned up. And alms — because alms is assistance for the poor. Not for us to live lavish lifestyles, not for us to drive in a Bentley and have a mansion and jet-set all over the world. When the Israelites collected alms, it was to do things beneficial for the healing of your nation, for the building of your nation. So he compares that to water putting out a fire, not you living lavishly with the church's money.

And alms maketh an atonement for sins. When you sin, God loves his people so much that you can give money to help your people, and God will see you have got mercy in your heart. You know you messed up. So that is why it is important that you understand what the alms is for, to make an atonement for your sin. And you have got to make sure the money is not being used in evil, it is being used to help your people. That is who you give alms to.

And he that requiteth good turns is mindful of that which may come hereafter; and when he falleth, he shall find a stay. When you fall, you will find a stay. Because the Most High will look and he will say, you know what — like with Manasseh. Remember Manasseh did much evil, but Manasseh still helped his people, so the Lord delivered him.
Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that ye may be safe.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: For the Lord hath given the father honour over the children, and hath confirmed the authority of the mother over the sons. That is saying a lot. It is telling us the order of the household, because a son about nine, ten years old, he starts to feel himself, and whoopings from mom, getting fussed at from mom, it starts to wear off. But that is when the dad steps in, hey listen, you do not talk to your mama like that, you do not deal with my wife like that. And it is teaching him the commandments. How do you discipline yourself when I am gone and out of town? You do not treat your mother like that. You have got to be who I am when I am not in the house. How can she trust you to take care of her when you are dealing with her wrongfully, when you are not honoring her?

Confirming that, son, no matter how old you are, you are never going to be older than your mama. Though you will be a ruler in Israel, you will never get to the age or position to disrespect your mom, to treat her less than you. She is always going to be the authority over you. And we constantly have to instill that into our sons, because our sons will overtake our women and they will get tired. Like, that is just what he is. They will make too much of their sons. They will let them do whatever they want to do because they cannot control them.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins: and he that honoureth his mother is as one that layeth up treasure. Because the Lord sees that. He sees how you treat your parents, how you treat the authority over you. And that authority is not just your own mother and father. It is your elders. It is the respect going back to our forefathers in the scriptures, because that is who we are listening to ultimately, what Moses wrote. We are showing our respect to his sacrifices. We are showing the respect of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, of what they instilled in us, that we rely on and respect them. We are taking the words of King Solomon and King David and saying, yes sir, I am going to do what you told me to do. And that ultimately goes to the ears and the eyes of the Lord, that we are going to listen to the Father that created us by listening to our parents.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children. Because you want that same respect, that reverence, from your own children. How can you get that respect out of your own kids when they see how you deal with your parents, how you talk to them, how you do or do not deal with them?
And when he maketh his prayer, he shall be heard.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: He that honoureth his father shall have a long life; and he that is obedient unto the Lord shall be a comfort to his mother.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: He that feareth the Lord will honour his father, and will do service unto his parents, as to his masters. He will do service unto his parents, meaning that they are going to obey. Yes sir, I am going to do that, I am on it. And that is teaching him how to govern his own life, because that masters part is going into, you are going to be a slave at some point. You are going to have to employ yourself. Even if you are an entrepreneur you are going to have to work for a living. You are going to be at somebody's service, providing services. You are going to have to deal with clients and customers. You are always going to have somebody ruling over you. So if you can do it with your parents, as much as it annoys you, bothers you, as painstaking as it is, the long suffering of being a kid trying to grow up, you are going to know how to be a servant. Because that is what it is, being a child. You are a servant to your parents, and they are teaching you how to be a servant in life, because you are going to be responsible for being a servant to God. It is all training to serve God. So if you can serve your parents at a child's level, then you can serve men at an adult level. And if you can serve God as an adult, then you can deal with the Most High and his chastening that comes with the consequences of your actions, whether they are good or bad.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: Honour thy father and mother both in word and deed. That is, in word and deed. You cannot be a respectful kid, yes sir, yes ma'am, but then not do what they say. That throws out the politeness. You can be the best at word, but it is the deeds that matter. How are you going to listen to somebody when I am telling you, when you see the trash can full and dirty, you have got to take the trash out and clean the mess on the trash can. When it is time for the trash truck to come, you have got to put it out that day or the night before, and you have to consistently do this. You have got to remember that this is your job, your duty to do. If you cannot listen to those instructions and those words and do that deed, how are you going to be an acceptable citizen? How are you going to be an acceptable servant to God?

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: That a blessing may come upon thee from them. For the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children. Just like we saw the example of the video of the two kids training from a child up. We have got to be the same thing in our words and our deeds to our children. Giving them the words, showing them how to do it, and then putting them to the test to do it, navigating them through the scriptures just the same as we are doing it. They should be the mirror of what we are righteously, because our mirror is our Father.
But the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: Glory not in the dishonour of thy father. Do not do that. Even if your parent in your eyes is not what they should be, you should not utter those words. Keep it within yourself and deal with the parents that you have got. Do not repeat their same steps, because that same thing that you put in your mind is going to stay with you, and you are going to rehearse it, and you are going to act out how you feel about your parents. And that acting out is going to spread to disrespect other elders. And now this kid is headstrong and cannot be told what to do, because they do not have respect for the adults that they have come up with.

The older he gets, the more tasks you put on him, because he is going to have to do it himself.
And grieve him not as long as he liveth.

points: And if his understanding fail, have patience with him. And that is the key thing. I want to get into repetition.

points: The heart of the prudent will understand a parable; and an attentive ear is the desire of a wise man. That is why we tell you to get your pen and notebook out and write scriptures. The ones looking around not paying attention, you already see what spirit is on them.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: He that requiteth good turns is mindful of that which may come hereafter; and when he falleth, he shall find a stay. We are all going to make mistakes, but if you keep a certain heart with God, when things go bad the Lord will sustain you. Never get to that place of pride where God says you are on your own.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Be not curious in unnecessary matters. This is not your business; stay in the scriptures. Feel sorry for neither the white man nor the Arab, since both had their hand in destroying our people; they can kill each other as long as they are not killing mine.

For more things are shewed unto thee than men understand. If you only know Deuteronomy 28 you know more than anyone outside this room. The media do not understand what is going on; America is trying to stop the prophecy with regime change, and it will not happen. You know the prophecy, so do not sleep.
Many are deceived by their own vain opinion, and an evil suspicion hath overthrown their judgment. Outside this Bible your opinion does not matter; God's word is where the power is.

A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last, and he that loveth danger shall perish therein. We have to prophesy against the idolatry and come out of Christmas, Valentine's Day and the rest that God never gave us.
Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that ye may be safe. So do thereafter that you may be safe.
For the Lord hath given the father honour over the children. And hath confirmed the authority of the mother over the sons.

Meaning what? Your parents look after you. You are supposed to listen to them. They have control over your life until you become a man. As a man, you become a man, you create your own household. But you still have got to honour and love them. You still have got to respect them according to the scriptures.
Whoso honoureth his father — whosoever honoureth his father, and your mother of course — maketh an atonement for his sins.
You make an atonement for your sins when you do that. When you honour your father, that wipes away your sins. Let us see why.

So when you honour your father, you make that atonement for your sins. And he that honoureth his mother, that respects his mother, is as one that layeth up treasure. You are as one that layeth up treasure.

Now, we are not talking about gold or diamonds or crypto or NFTs. Let us see what type of treasure the Bible is talking about that you lay up for yourself when you honour your father and respect your mother.

Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children. Whoso honoureth his father will have joy of his own children. And when he maketh his prayer. And when he what? When he maketh his prayer, he shall be heard.

So when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard. So why does it say that? It means when you are not honouring your father or your mother, your prayers are not going to be heard. Showing that it is a commandment to honour your parents. Why is that? Why will your prayers not be heard?
He that honoureth his father shall have a long life. He that honoureth his father will have a long life. And not just this life, in the next life too.
And he that is obedient unto the Lord. And he that is what? That is obedient unto the Lord. If you are obedient to the Lord and to what it says in the scriptures, shall be a comfort to his mother.

You are automatically going to be a comfort to your mother, because the way you move, the way you speak to people, the way you treat your family members is going to show that in your actions. A lot of us came into the truth and your family was like, you know what, I do not agree with, you know, it is only the Jews, it is only this, the commandments, all this and that, but I cannot say nothing against you, you have gotten so much better as a person. And if you have not heard that, at least some form of that, then you might not be repenting, right?
He that feareth the Lord will honour his father. He that feareth the Lord will honour his father. And will do service unto his parents, as to his masters.
So the same respect that you should have for your boss or your employer, or whoever is over you, whoever gainfully employs you, you should have that same respect and more for your parents.

The same way we have respect for our elders, for the men over us, or whoever you report to, you need to have that same respect or more for your parents as well too, because they brought you into this world.
Honour thy father and mother. Both in word and deed. Both in word and deed. Meaning whatever you say, do it. That a blessing may come upon thee. From them. From them.

What type of blessing is that? For the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations. But the curse of the mother can root out foundations.
How can the blessings of a father establish children? Let us see. But you can only get this blessing if you are honouring and respecting your parents and doing what the Lord says to do.
For the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.

The curse of the mother. If you are not respecting and honouring your mother, like it says in the commandments, those curses are going to come upon you. You are going to have holes in your pockets. You are going to be afflicted for breaking that commandment. And back in the day children were put to death for dishonouring their father and mother. So thank God that the Most High sent his son, because a lot of us would be dead, and a lot of these children would have been stoned expeditiously for the way these kids act nowadays.
For thy father's dishonour is no glory unto thee. There is no glory unto you when your father is in dishonour. You came from him.

Glory not in the dishonour of thy father. Glory not in the dishonour of thy father. Oh, my dad, yeah man, he is broke, he is a bum now, he is x, y and z, my mom left him behind. That is no glory to you.

For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father. For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father. And a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children. And a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.

My son, help thy father in his age. My son. So we all have got to help our fathers and mothers in their old age, when they become like a baby again. Once a man, twice a child. When they start acting funny, when they lose their wits about them and they start doing crazy things. You have got to help them when it comes to moving, when it comes to their finances, when it comes to life decisions. You have got to help them the same way they helped you when you were a kid with no sense, when you did not have any rhyme or reason, and how they guided you. Now you have to guide them in their old age when they start losing their wits, because it happens to a lot of our people.
And grieve him not as long as he liveth. And grieve him not. Do not be a grievance to him as long as he liveth.

And if his understanding fail — that is what I was talking about, when people lose their wits, when their understanding fails — have patience with him. We have got to have patience with them. The same way Christ had patience with us when we were sinning willingly all about.

And despise him not when thou art in thy full strength. And despise him not. Do not despise your parents now. Oh, I am doing better, I am married, I have got a good job, I am in the truth. And you are looking down at them with your nose in the air. The Bible does not say to do that.

For the relieving of thy father shall not be forgotten. For the relieving of thy father shall not be forgotten. I mean, in all the commandments, all the things of the scriptures that we applied towards our fathers and our mothers, the Lord is not going to forget that. Like it says back in verse three, that is going to make an atonement for our sins. And remember, how we treat our brother and sister is how we treat who? Christ. So just because they are not repentant does not mean that person does not come from the body of Christ.

And instead of sins it shall be added to build thee up. So instead of sins, it is going to be added in your good works to build you up. In the day of thine affliction it shall be remembered. Thy sins also shall melt away, as the ice in the fair warm weather.
He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer. He that forsaketh his father is a blasphemer. And he that angereth his mother is cursed of God. And he that angereth his mother is cursed of God.
